Source: https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2026/Oct/29
Published PoC: Exploit-Garbage/0day-Rubbish, product/edimax/br-6478ac-v2.20/setwan-command-injection-root-rce.

These fixtures reconstruct the disclosed WAN-configuration username shell injection,
not the vulnerable firmware. No requests were sent to a device. The author dynamically
replicated only the PPP sink locally; PPTP/L2TP are static analysis claims.

The five hostile fixtures exercise pipe/ampersand command breakout, output capture
and suffix commenting over PPP/PPTP/L2TP, including URL-encoded wire data.
The three suspicious fixtures exercise dollar-parentheses, backticks and newlines.
Each carries the actual wanMode and submit-url fields of the protocol.

Benign fixtures cover ordinary configuration submissions, punctuation inside scalar
credentials, ordinary shell pipelines, shell task fields and unrelated payload text.
They must produce no suspicious or hostile findings.

The hostile rules add HTTP/WAN-form context to product-independent credential
injection syntax. Generic program execution, theft, persistence, privilege escalation,
firmware compromise and researcher-domain identity are not inferred.
